newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICAN MINERS ASK GOVT TO EYE PESO APPRECIATION.
newsitem.headline: MEXICAN MINERS ASK GOVT TO EYE PESO APPRECIATION.

text.p: The Mexican Mining Chamber Tuesday praised the government for its attempts to prevent the peso from appreciating but warned that foreign exchange levels needed careful watching to avoid hurting exporters.

Chairman Eduardo Luna said at the inauguration of the chamber's annual meeting that the central bank's efforts were "laudable" in its bid to stop the peso gaining against the dollar despite strong hard currency inflows.

"Mining continues moving forward in spite of problems such as the foreigh exchange rate which does not reflect the difference there is in inflation between our country and our main business partners," Luna said.

Luna, speaking before President Ernesto Zedillo, said the Banco de Mexico's recent attempts to cap even more peso strength by increasing the amount of its monthly dollar put auctions were praiseworthy.

"The exchange rate is a point that has to receive a lot of attention so that the export sector is not punished because that very sector is the dynamic one and leading the recovery of our economy," Luna said.

Widespread concern has been voiced in recent weeks over Mexico's peso and its stubborn resistance to weakening against the dollar despite inflation major differences between Mexico and the United States
Economists reckon the peso is around 10 percent overvalued, a factor which hurts dollar earning export companies, including miners.
